finding_1_f5_numerator.internal_inconsistency: the same page pair prints x = f/g = (Theta w)^-1 + (3/(10*4!))(Theta w)^4 + ... and g/(1-w)^2 = (Theta w) - (3/6!)(Theta w)^6 - ... .  Expanding x = f/g gives x_4 = f_5 - g_6, hence f_5 = x_4 + g_6 = 1/80 - 1/240 = 1/120 = 1/5!.
finding_1_f5_numerator.conclusion: the displayed numerator 120 must be 1.  With f_5 = 1/5! all eleven of our parameter-free invariants match the printed f, g, x and phi coefficients to <= 1.072e-21; with the displayed 120 they miss by factors of exactly (5!)^m.
finding_1_f5_numerator.independent_confirmation: our own computation, which never used the printed f_5, agrees with the corrected value.

finding_2_phi_formula.objection: on y^2 = x^6 - x/6 the point (0,0) is a Weierstrass point at which x vanishes to order 2, so x^3 vanishes to order 6 while y+1 -> 1.  Hence (y+1)/(2x^3) has degree 6 and cannot be the degree-5 Belyi map.
finding_2_phi_formula.repair: (y+x^3)/(2x^3) has divisor 5*inf_- - 5*(0,0) and (phi-1) has divisor 5*inf_+ - 5*(0,0); its expansion at w = 0 begins (1/24)(Theta w)^5, exactly the printed phi(w).  The displayed 1 should be x^3.

machine_confirmation.reading: (y+x^3)/(2x^3) built from OUR series is lacunary mod 5 to 6.3e-76 -- i.e. it is Delta-invariant, as a Galois Belyi map must be -- and its three leading coefficients reproduce the printed phi(w) parameter-free.  (y+1)/(2x^3) is neither.

step_4_shape_of_Q_and_C.prediction_Q: Q = alpha e_1^2 + gamma e_2^2 + delta e_3 e_4 ; the (1,2),(1,3),(1,4),(2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(4,4) entries of the 4x4 symmetric matrix all VANISH.  delta != 0 (else Q has rank <= 2 = a pair of planes, impossible for a canonical curve).  rank Q = 2 + #{alpha != 0} + #{gamma != 0}: rank 4 iff both nonzero (two g^1_3), rank 3 iff exactly one vanishes (one g^1_3).
step_4_shape_of_Q_and_C.invariant_cubics: (Sym^3 V)^{S_3} = <e_1^3, e_1 e_2^2, e_1 e_3 e_4, e_3^3 + e_4^3>, dimension 4; e_1*Q lies in the span of the first three

step_4_shape_of_Q_and_C.honest_caveat: the EXISTENCE of an order-3 isometry of Q alone is not a constraint on Q (every smooth quadric has many).  The content of the test is the JOINT condition A*Q = Q and A*C = C mod V*Q, which is what part_S3_numerical measures.

step_5_the_involution_iota.status: POST-HOC -- this derivation was made AFTER the Sym^2 kernel was first printed, when the sparsity of Q was noticed.  It is a derivation from pre-registered inputs, not a fitted parameter, and it is reported as post-hoc.
step_5_the_involution_iota.statement: the transposition of S_3 that fixes the branch point 0 fixes the point P_0 (sigma_0 is a 9-cycle, so the fibre over 0 is a single point).  An automorphism of X fixing P_0 lifts to an isometry of H fixing z_a, i.e. a rotation, i.e. w -> lambda w with |lambda| = 1; for an involution lambda = -1.  Since omega = f dz = 2i S(w) dw for weight 2 (the VW factor (1-w)^2 is exactly dz/dw), the pullback acts on the series by S(u) -> -S(-u), i.e. btilde_n -> (-1)^(n+1) btilde_n.
step_5_the_involution_iota.consequences: f_1, f_3 are EVEN series and f_2, f_4 are ODD series; the echelon basis is automatically an eigenbasis with iota = diag(-1,+1,-1,+1); the (+1)-eigenspace <f_2,f_4> has dimension 2 = g(X/C_2), an independent confirmation of spec sec.3.5's F_tau = 2; and Q, being S_3-invariant, must have vanishing coefficients on X1X2, X1X4, X2X3, X3X4.

part_L6_step1_Sym2.why_evaluations: ben3 U-D3.  The contribution of btilde_n to f(u) is btilde_n (|u|/rho)^n, so |u| <= 0.68 rho suppresses the least accurate tail; the coefficient-truncation scan below shows the answer is already converged at n_max = 240.

part_S3_numerical.what: the numerical counterpart of part_paper_derivation_S3, and the geometric half of spec [G6'-c] item 3 (formally ben6's task; delivered here as a by-product because iota made it cheap)
part_S3_numerical.reduction: A has eigenvalues (1,1,omega,omega^2) and A*Q = Q, so its omega- and omega^2-eigenlines are Q-ISOTROPIC and its 1-eigenplane is their Q-orthogonal complement.  Conversely ANY pair of lines <v_-> in <f_1,f_3>, <v_+> in <f_2,f_4> determines such an A with A*Q = Q automatically.  The entire test therefore reduces to TWO complex parameters and the single question: is C o A equal to C modulo V*Q?  That is 16 complex equations in 2 complex unknowns.
part_S3_numerical.verdict: a UNIQUE order-3 A exists (one solution from 600 random starts), its eigenvalue multiplicities are (2,1,1) as Chevalley-Weil predicts, it satisfies iota A iota = A^(-1) to 3.65e-16 so <A, iota> is a genuine S_3 inside PGL_4 preserving the standard model, and C o A = 1 * C modulo V*Q -- i.e. BOTH Q AND C ARE S_3-INVARIANT, exactly as the paper derivation predicted before the search was written.

unknowns.text: The iota-symmetry (part_paper_derivation_S3 step 5) was derived AFTER the Sym^2 kernel was printed.  It is a derivation from pre-registered inputs (spec sec.3.5 + the echelon pivots), and it is confirmed independently by the 1e-73 parity of the ben2 basis coefficients, which were fixed before ben4 began.  But it was not pre-registered, and it is labelled post-hoc throughout.

rank Q = 4 rests on the smallest singular value of the normalised 4x4 matrix being 0.1447, seven orders above the floor, and being identical at N = 538 and N = 717.  That is strong, but the rank of a numerically computed matrix is not a proved statement; a rank-3 curve whose quadric is within 1e-16 of rank 4 is not excluded by this evidence alone (it is excluded by the S_3 eigenbasis, where alpha, gamma, delta are all O(1) after normalisation -- but that too is numerical).

The essential cubic C is unique only modulo V*Q, and the representative reported is fixed by an orthogonality convention in the monomial coordinates.  Any downstream statement about the COEFFICIENTS of C must either quotient by V*Q or declare the same convention.  The reduction inside the S_3 eigenbasis (part_S3_numerical) shows how much the representative moves: two of the four reduction coefficients are 4.5e-3, not negligible.

The order-3 A was found by multi-start Gauss-Newton in ComplexF64, not by an exhaustive argument.  600 starts produced exactly one solution, and the parametrisation misses the measure-zero charts v_- proportional to f_3 and v_+ proportional to f_4, so 'unique' means 'unique in the chart searched, with 600 starts'.  The paper derivation says an order-3 A exists; the search confirms it and measures it; the two together do not constitute a proof of uniqueness.

The two printed-value findings against KMSV Example 5.26 are established from the printed data alone and are internally consistent with our computation, but Example 5.26 was NOT part of the pre-registered CAL (that was Example 5.27, ben3).  It is a second calibration point added by ruling 1803(b), and the quarantine rule is applied by analogy, not by the letter of spec sec.5.

L6' remains an UNCALIBRATED layer in the sense of ben3's U-D5: no public genus-4 solution exists (BelyiDB has 6 genus-4 entries, none with a computed Belyi map).  What ben4 adds is (a) a second uniformisation calibration at genus 2 that exercises L1'-L5' end to end against a published answer, (b) a synthetic positive control for the genus-4 discriminator, (c) five structure predictions derived on paper and confirmed, and (d) a destruction control that locates the detector's sensitivity.  It is not the same as a public genus-4 solution.
